correctness.rationale: Classical 123 avoidance with linear jumps |π_(i+1)-π_i|≤m implies π_1≥n−m: the first subsequent term above π_1 must be n, and its predecessor is at most π_1 but within m of n. Applying reverse-complement gives π_n≤m+1. The cyclic closing jump then imposes n−2m−1≤π_1−π_n≤m, hence n≤3m+1; m=1 cannot host an n≥3 simple Hamiltonian cycle. For m≥2 the displayed five-block witness W_m at n=3m+1 is a permutation, 123-avoiding, has maximal edge jump m including its closing edge. For 5≤n<3m+1 choose r=ceil((n−1)/3)≤m and delete 0,1,2 largest entries from W_r; new jumps stay ≤r; n=3,4 use explicit tuples. At equality all endpoint inequalities are equalities; the first exceeding n−m is n immediately after π_1, and reversed complement forces π_(n−1)=1. This proves every claimed quantifier and boundary. Independent direct permutation enumeration compared all 24 pairs (n=3..8,m=1..4), forced endpoints and exact existence, with no counterexample. These tests are finite; the all-parameter proof is the endpoint argument and construction.
